title: Skin Lesions
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with fragile skin, blistering lesions on sun-exposed areas (hands, face, forearms), milia, hyperpigmentation, and hypertrichosis. PCT is the most common porphyria — caused by deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase (UROD) → accumulation of uroporphyrins in skin → photosensitivity. Acquired form associated with: alcohol, hepatitis C, HIV, hemochromatosis, estrogen therapy. Diagnosis: elevated uroporphyrins and heptacarboxyl porphyrins in urine, plasma porphyrins (peak at 620nm), stool isocoproporphyrin. Treatment: phlebotomy (remove iron — goal ferritin low-normal) or low-dose hydroxychloroquine (mobilizes porphyrins). Avoid sun exposure, alcohol, and estrogens. Screen for HCV, HIV, hemochromatosis.
